question: When do midwives usually perform the first check of a newborn boy's external genitalia?

options.C: At six weeks of postnatal life
options.D: Only if the mother requests it

explanation: Midwives perform a newborn physical check shortly after birth to confirm normal development and catch any issues early. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T1#BMP210_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why do midwifery students learn the anatomy of the male external genitalia?

options.B: To perform surgical corrections in the labor ward
options.C: To prescribe hormonal treatments for newborns
options.D: To accurately identify normal structures and spot congenital abnormalities

explanation: Knowing normal anatomy helps midwives recognize variations, reassure parents, and make timely referrals when needed. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T1#BMP210_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is the name of the tough fibrous layer that encloses the erectile tissue inside the penis?
explanation: The tunica albuginea is a strong fibrous sheath that wraps around the erectile tissue columns within the penile shaft. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T1#BMP210_U3_T1_h2)

question: Which specific structure contains the spongy urethra inside the shaft of the penis?
explanation: The corpus spongiosum runs along the underside of the penis and surrounds the urethra as it travels toward the tip. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T1#BMP210_U3_T1_h2)

question: Which part of the nervous system triggers the relaxation of penile blood vessels to produce an erection?
explanation: Parasympathetic nerve signals cause blood vessels in the erectile tissue to widen, allowing blood to fill the chambers. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T1#BMP210_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the term for the process where rhythmic muscle contractions in the pelvis expel semen?
explanation: Ejaculation is the expulsion of semen driven by coordinated muscular contractions in the pelvic region. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T1#BMP210_U3_T1_h3)

question: Why does the scrotum keep the testes at a slightly lower temperature than core body heat?
explanation: Normal sperm development requires a cooler environment than the internal body temperature provides. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T1#BMP210_U3_T1_h4)

question: What does the cremaster muscle do when the body is exposed to a cold environment?

options.A: It relaxes to let the testes hang lower
options.B: It pulls the testes closer to the body wall
options.C: It closes the inguinal canal completely
options.D: It flattens the scrotal skin to release sweat

explanation: The cremaster muscle reflexively contracts in response to cold to keep the testes warm near the pelvic cavity. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T1#BMP210_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the name of the fibrous cord that guides the testes downward during fetal development?
explanation: The gubernaculum acts as a guide, pulling the testis from the abdomen down through the canal and into the scrotum. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T1#BMP210_U3_T1_h5)

question: A preterm baby boy is born at 32 weeks, and his scrotal sacs feel empty and cannot be felt. What is the best initial action for the midwife?

options.A: Document the finding and monitor during routine postnatal visits
options.B: Perform an immediate surgical repositioning procedure
options.D: Tell the mother the condition is permanent and untreatable

explanation: Many preterm infants experience delayed descent that corrects itself over the first few months, so monitoring is the appropriate step. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T1#BMP210_U3_T1_h5)

question: Where is the opening of the urethra located in a newborn with hypospadias?

options.A: On the dorsal top surface of the penis
options.B: Inside the perineal raphe behind the scrotum
options.C: On the ventral underside of the penis
options.D: Directly at the center of the glans tip

explanation: Hypospadias happens when the urethral tube does not close all the way to the tip, leaving the opening on the underside. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T1#BMP210_U3_T1_h6)

question: What physical sign helps a midwife tell a simple hydrocele apart from other scrotal swellings?

options.A: It transilluminates brightly when a light source is applied
options.B: It causes severe acute pain in the neonate
options.C: It feels hard and bony upon palpation
options.D: It disappears completely when the infant cries

explanation: Because a hydrocele is filled with clear fluid, light passes through it easily, lighting up the scrotum during transillumination. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T1#BMP210_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why is it important to examine a newborn boy in a warm room?

options.A: To keep the vernix caseosa from drying out too quickly
options.B: To prevent the cremasteric reflex from pulling the testes upward
options.C: To stop the infant from crying during the examination
options.D: To ensure the urethral meatus dilates fully

explanation: Cold air triggers the cremaster muscle to contract, pulling the testes up and making them hard to feel during the check. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T1#BMP210_U3_T1_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT part of a standard newborn genital check for a male infant?

options.A: Measuring the exact length of the vas deferens
options.B: Palpating both halves of the scrotal sac
options.C: Checking the position of the urethral meatus
options.D: Inspecting the penis for abnormal curvature or swelling

explanation: The vas deferens is an internal duct deep inside the spermatic cord and cannot be measured during a routine external newborn exam. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T1#BMP210_U3_T1_h7)
